w:r.w:t: FUNCTIONAL, NON-FUNCTIONAL, TECHNICAL AND TESTABLE REQUIREMENTS
Prepared for startup pitching, product planning and engineering execution.

This SRS defines the software behavior and quality requirements for SocietyOS. It translates the startup proposal into implementable, testable requirements. The SRS is intended to be the contract between product decisions, UI/UX work, backend implementation and QA.
Society/tenant management; units and residents; role/permission management.
Visitor passes, approvals and gate check-in/out.
Complaints, maintenance work orders, assignment, attachments and status tracking.
Maintenance billing records, payment evidence, receipts and outstanding balances.
Announcements and notification delivery through provider adapters.
Admin dashboards, search, filtering, reports and audit logs.
AI-assisted classification, summaries and authorized information retrieval.
Security, validation, observability, testing and deployment requirements.
Tenant lifecycle, support access with audit trail, system configuration
Residents, units, staff, visitors, complaints, bills, notices, reports, audit
View valid passes, verify visitor, check in/out, incident entry
Accept, update and complete work orders; upload evidence
Visitors, complaints, service requests, bills, notices, profile
Bills, receipts, payment records, reports, adjustments per policy
V1 is a responsive web application; native mobile apps are out of scope until API contracts are stable.
MongoDB is the primary application datastore; Cloudinary handles media/file storage.
Email and WhatsApp are provider-based integrations; provider outages must not corrupt application state.
AI is an assistive subsystem with explicit authorization boundaries.
The application is multi-tenant; cross-tenant data access is prohibited by default.
V1 is not a banking platform and does not hold customer funds; payment behavior is represented through payment records, evidence and provider adapters.
The system shall authenticate users using approved credential flows and shall reject disabled or unauthorized accounts.
The system shall issue short-lived access credentials and maintain a secure refresh-session mechanism.
The system shall enforce role and permission checks on every protected API operation.
Every society-scoped record shall be associated with a tenantId.
Repository operations shall apply tenant scope by default.
Admins shall create, update, suspend and search resident records within their tenant.
Admins shall manage blocks/buildings, units, occupancy state and resident relationships.
Residents shall create visitor passes with expected visitor details, date/time window and optional notes.
Authorized society staff shall approve/reject passes according to configured policy.
Security staff shall check in only valid, approved, currently usable passes.
The system shall record check-in and checkout actor/timestamps and preserve an audit trail.
Residents and staff shall create complaints with category, description, priority context and optional attachments.
The system shall support complaint state transitions: OPEN → TRIAGED → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED, with governed reopen/cancel paths.
Each status transition shall record actor, timestamp, previous state and optional note.
Maintenance supervisors shall assign work orders to eligible staff.
Maintenance staff shall update work order progress and attach completion evidence.
Finance staff shall generate bills and maintain outstanding balances for a unit/resident.
The system shall preserve adjustment/reversal history rather than silently changing financial history.
The system shall create notification events for configured business triggers.
Provider adapters shall support email and WhatsApp without embedding provider-specific logic in domain services.
AI classification/summarization requests shall be initiated through an internal service boundary.
AI shall not directly execute high-impact actions such as visitor approval, bill waiver, record deletion or permission changes.
The system shall record audit events for security-sensitive and materially consequential administrative actions.
Admins shall access dashboards showing relevant operational metrics only for authorized tenant scope.
List endpoints shall support pagination; unbounded collection responses shall be prohibited.
Uploads shall be validated for MIME type, size and permitted use; storage shall use signed/safe Cloudinary flows.
No tenant data shall be returned to a request whose tenant context is unauthorized.
Passwords shall use a modern password hashing algorithm; secrets shall never be committed to source control.
Protected endpoints shall apply rate limits appropriate to login, reset/OTP and expensive AI operations.
Error responses shall not expose stack traces, secrets or internal database details.
Primary list screens shall be paginated and indexed according to measured query patterns.
External notification/AI failures shall be observable and retryable where the operation is safe to retry.
Primary workflows shall be keyboard usable, focus-visible and readable without relying only on color.
Core resident/security workflows shall work without horizontal scroll on intended mobile breakpoints.
Controllers translate HTTP; services own business rules; repositories own persistence.
Each request shall receive a requestId and safe structured logs shall include route, status and duration.
Critical business workflows shall have automated integration and end-to-end coverage.
Production builds shall be reproducible through CI/CD with environment-specific secrets and health checks.
Use a restrained premium visual system: generous spacing, strong typography, quiet surfaces and meaningful motion.
Every major screen shall have a clear title, primary action, search/filter behavior where relevant, and useful empty/loading/error states.
High-frequency resident actions shall be one or two interactions away on mobile.
Status labels and domain vocabulary shall be consistent across roles.
Destructive actions shall state the consequence and require confirmation when appropriate.
Permission-denied and unavailable states shall explain why an action is unavailable without leaking security details.
No dashboard metric shall exist only for decoration; every KPI must answer an operational question.
OPEN → TRIAGED → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED; governed reopen/cancel transitions only.
DRAFT → REQUESTED → APPROVED / REJECTED → ARRIVED → CHECKED_IN → CHECKED_OUT → EXPIRED.
QUEUED → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → BLOCKED / WAITING_PARTS → COMPLETED → VERIFIED.
DRAFT → ISSUED → PARTIALLY_PAID → PAID / OVERDUE → VOID; history is adjustment-based, not silent overwrite.
Authenticated request context must include userId + tenantId; repositories scope by tenant by default.
Every materially consequential state change captures actor + timestamp + previous/new state where applicable.

No sensitive prompt retention beyond policy
Base path: /api/v1. Use plural resource names, predictable HTTP status codes, machine-readable error codes, and consistent pagination/filtering patterns. Controllers must not query MongoDB directly.
AI should be invoked only for defined product use cases, not as a universal text box with uncontrolled database access.
Every AI tool call must run with authenticated tenant/user context and explicit permission checks.
AI responses that involve live records must be grounded in authorized tool results rather than fabricated values.
High-impact actions require deterministic business rules and explicit user confirmation.
Prompts, model choices and tool contracts shall be versioned enough to reproduce behavior during testing.
AI failures should degrade gracefully to normal product workflows.
Argon2id or equivalent modern password hashing.
HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite-aware refresh session strategy; strict CORS.
Rate limits for authentication, reset/OTP and expensive AI endpoints.
Server-side validation, unknown-field rejection where appropriate, safe error mapping.
Security headers / Helmet and deployment-appropriate CSP.
MIME/size/extension validation for uploads; signed access to stored files.
Tenant isolation tests attempting cross-tenant reads/writes.
Audit events for permission changes, user status changes, bills/payments, visitor approvals and administrative operations.
Services, state transitions, policies, validation and pure domain functions.
Repositories + database, auth/permission middleware, critical API modules, notification adapters.
Resident creates visitor; security checks in; complaint progresses; maintenance completes work order; bill flow; representative AI retrieval.
Auth abuse, privilege escalation, tenant isolation, input validation, file upload, rate limiting.
Keyboard navigation, focus order, labels, error association, contrast/readability checks.
List endpoints, dashboards, common search/filter queries and concurrent high-frequency actions.
Full automated suite on protected branches + manual smoke on staging/production releases.
Correct user role reaches only authorized pages and APIs; refresh/logout behavior is safe.
Resident sees only own profile/unit scope and can perform intended self-service actions.
Invalid/expired/unapproved passes cannot be checked in; all transitions are auditable.
Status transitions follow policy; assignment and history are visible to authorized users.
Work order evidence and completion state are recorded and visible to correct parties.
Amounts, status and adjustments are traceable; financial history is not silently overwritten.
Trigger produces a notification event and provider result; failures are observable.
Only authorized data is used; high-impact actions remain deterministic and human-confirmed.
Dashboard metrics are tenant-scoped and consistent with underlying data queries.
CI passes; health/readiness checks succeed; logs/monitoring are active; rollback/restore procedure documented.
Real database persistence; no permanent mock data.
Backend authorization is enforced and UI reflects permissions.
Tenant isolation is proven by automated tests.
Validation and consistent errors exist at API boundary.
At least one automated business-rule test exists for each meaningful workflow.
No known release-blocking console errors or unhandled promise warnings.
Responsive behavior verified at intended breakpoints.
API/schema/architecture docs updated with significant changes.
Lint, typecheck, tests and production build pass.
Testing, security, observability and deployment acceptance
